builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: DocSkill: Skill-Integrated Agentic Reasoning for Multilingual Multi-Hop Document Question Answering
summary: DocSkill replaces single-pass document processing and hand-designed adaptive tool-use pipelines with a learned policy that selects, revisits, or skips skills (evidence acquisition, cross-page integration, verification) based on the evolving evidence state, trained via offline bounded MCTS to generate SFT demonstrations and DPO preference pairs. Adopting it costs an offline MCTS trajectory-search phase, supervised fine-tuning plus DPO on a vision-language model (feasible for an 8B model on a 24 GB GPU only with parameter-efficient methods and quantized inference), and a new training dataset built by the paper's HopGen page-element graph pipeline, which adds substantial engineering complexity. It can fail because the learned orchestration policy is trained on the authors' MMHop-DocBench distribution and may not transfer to other document domains, languages, or skill sets without re-collecting MCTS trajectories, and the gains are demonstrated only against baselines the authors evaluated on their own new benchmark.
rationale: The method requires an offline MCTS search pipeline, a custom dataset-generation pipeline, and SFT-plus-DPO training of a vision-language model, which exceeds typical constrained-infrastructure adoption effort, and its quality gains are benchmark-specific and unproven for general workloads, so it warrants monitoring rather than immediate adoption.
technique: Learned skill-orchestration policy for agentic document QA

claims.statement: DocSkill replaces single-pass document processing and hand-designed adaptive tool-use pipelines with a learned policy that selects, revisits, or skips skills (evidence acquisition, cross-page integration, verification) based on the evolving evidence state, trained via offline bounded MCTS to generate SFT demonstrations and DPO preference pairs. Adopting it costs an offline MCTS trajectory-search phase, supervised fine-tuning plus DPO on a vision-language model (feasible for an 8B model on a 24 GB GPU only with parameter-efficient methods and quantized inference), and a new training dataset built by the paper's HopGen page-element graph pipeline, which adds substantial engineering complexity. It can fail because the learned orchestration policy is trained on the authors' MMHop-DocBench distribution and may not transfer to other document domains, languages, or skill sets without re-collecting MCTS trajectories, and the gains are demonstrated only against baselines the authors evaluated on their own new benchmark.

DocSkill with Qwen3-VL-8B achieves 41.0 accuracy and 49.2 F1 on MMHop-DocBench, exceeding the strongest evaluated baseline by 5.5 and 6.3 points respectively, with competitive results on MMLongBench-Doc and DocBench; these are absolute point gains, not multiplicative factors.
